definitions.explanation: A printed sheet of paper distributed to advertise events, products, or causes. Often handed out on the street or posted on walls.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}る→配る：03921_kubaru⟧。
examples.english: To hand out flyers in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦イベント→イベント：09594_ibento⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{掲示板|けいじばん}→掲示板：03052_keijiban⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{貼|は}った→貼る：10447_haru⟧。
examples.english: I made flyers for the event and put them on the bulletin board.

examples.japanese: ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}された→渡す：02442_watasu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{読|よ}ま→読む：00426_yomu⟧ず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{捨|す}てた→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧。
examples.english: A stranger on the street handed me a flyer, but I threw it away without reading it.

notes:
USAGE:
ビラ is a somewhat dated word compared to ⟦チラシ→チラシ：23406_chirashi⟧, which is the more common term for advertising flyers. ビラ tends to appear in contexts involving political leaflets, protest materials, or street-level distribution, while ⟦チラシ→チラシ：23406_chirashi⟧ is more neutral and commercial.

ETYMOLOGY:
From Portuguese "bilhete" (ticket/note) or possibly a Japanese onomatopoeia for things fluttering.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}る→配る：03921_kubaru⟧: to hand out flyers
- ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撒|ま}く→撒く：12711_maku⟧: to scatter/distribute flyers
- ビラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}る→貼る：10447_haru⟧: to post flyers
